title: Onboard a repository
summary: Discover the map, commands and policy before touching code.
when: A new repository, a stale summary, or an unfamiliar module.

steps.title: Read the policy
steps.body: Read AGENTS.md first, then the build manifests and the pull-request workflow.
steps.done: Commands are sourced from the repository, not invented.

steps.title: Build the map
steps.body: Inventory stacks, modules, tests, CI and interface candidates with the dependency-free detector.
steps.done: The map cites paths and marks its inferences.

steps.title: Install the controls
steps.body: If the repository has no `.agents/engineering.json`, install the kit and commit the resulting files.
steps.done: The config and AGENTS section are reviewed; hooks are enabled locally.

steps.title: Run the baseline
steps.body: Run the fast gate before editing and record pre-existing failures separately.
steps.done: A baseline evidence record exists and failures are known.

title: Fix a bug
summary: Reproduce, prove the cause, fix it, and leave a red-then-green test.
when: A failing test, crash, incident or reported behavior.

steps.title: Reproduce
steps.body: Capture the exact command, revision, environment and full failure. Reduce the input while it still fails.
steps.done: The smallest failing reproduction is recorded.

steps.title: Establish the baseline
steps.body: Run the existing suite and record pre-existing failures. Do not attribute them to the fix.
steps.done: Baseline results are saved.

steps.title: Write the regression test
steps.body: Add the test to the existing file for the area. Prove it fails on the unfixed revision for the reported reason.
steps.done: The test fails before the fix with the expected assertion.

steps.title: Fix the cause
steps.body: Make the smallest change that removes the cause, not the symptom. Do not combine it with a refactor.
steps.done: The reproduction and the new test pass.

steps.title: Verify and report
steps.body: Run the targeted test, the fast gate and the required full gate. Report the evidence id and residual risk.
steps.done: Evidence is pass or an explicit blocked/skip is reported.

title: Add a feature
summary: Turn an outcome into the smallest change with a testable contract.
when: A new user-visible capability, command, endpoint or setting.

steps.title: Define the acceptance criteria
steps.body: Write what the user can observe, including defaults, errors and compatibility. Separate must-haves from preferences.
steps.done: Criteria are testable and the affected consumers are listed.

steps.title: Design the smallest interface
steps.body: Prefer an existing pattern to a new abstraction. Name the contract and its owner.
steps.done: The interface and compatibility decision are explicit.

steps.title: Implement with tests
steps.body: Add unit tests for the new behavior and integration tests at the real boundary. Keep unrelated refactors out.
steps.done: The new tests fail without the change and pass with it.

steps.title: Check the contract and security
steps.body: Add old/new fixtures for serialization, CLI output or schema changes. Run the relevant scanners.
steps.done: Compatibility and security checks are recorded.

steps.title: Ship with evidence
steps.body: Report the behavior, commands, skips and residual risk. Link the evidence record.
steps.done: A reviewer can reproduce the verification.

title: Refactor safely
summary: Change structure without changing observable behavior.
when: Extracting modules, renaming internals, removing duplication or preparing for a feature.

steps.title: Freeze the behavior
steps.body: Run the relevant tests and add characterization or golden coverage where it is thin.
steps.done: The baseline is green or known failures are documented.

steps.title: Identify the contract
steps.body: List public symbols, serialized output, errors, defaults and performance that must not change.
steps.done: The observable surface is named.

steps.title: Move in small steps
steps.body: One mechanical step at a time. Run the compiler and narrow tests after each step.
steps.done: Each step is reviewable and green.

steps.title: Compare behavior
steps.body: Run the contract and characterization fixtures. Compare performance on hot paths.
steps.done: Outputs are identical; any change is explicit.

steps.title: Separate the discovery
steps.body: If the refactor reveals a bug, record it and open a separate change. Do not silently expand scope.
steps.done: New issues have their own evidence and owner.

title: Harden a surface
summary: Model the trust boundary, scan it, fix the cause, and prove the fix.
when: Input parsing, auth, secrets, subprocesses, files, network, CI permissions or a scanner finding.

steps.title: Map the trust boundary
steps.body: Name the assets, actors, entry points, privileged operations and attacker-controlled data.
steps.done: The boundary and preconditions are explicit.

steps.title: Run the scanners
steps.body: Run secrets, SAST, dependency, workflow and pin checks. Read the findings, not only the counts.
steps.done: Every finding has a location and a decision.

steps.title: Fix or suppress narrowly
steps.body: Fix the cause. A false positive gets an exact, reviewed suppression with a reason; never broaden the rule.
steps.done: The scanner is clean or the exception is justified.

steps.title: Add a regression test
steps.body: Test the exploit precondition and the rejection. Do not publish exploit details in a public issue.
steps.done: The test fails on the vulnerable revision and passes after.

title: Improve performance
summary: Baseline, profile, change one thing, and measure the distribution.
when: Latency, throughput, memory, startup or build-time work.

steps.title: Define the metric
steps.body: Choose the user-facing metric and a target. Pin the workload, hardware and build profile.
steps.done: The measurement is repeatable.

steps.title: Record the baseline
steps.body: Take at least five samples after warm-up. Keep the raw results and environment.
steps.done: Median, p95 and variance are recorded.

steps.title: Profile before changing
steps.body: Find the dominant cost. A small function is not the bottleneck just because it looks slow.
steps.done: The bottleneck has evidence.

steps.title: Change one thing
steps.body: Re-run the identical workload and check correctness and other metrics.
steps.done: The effect exceeds noise and correctness holds.

title: Parallelize work
summary: Split by independently verifiable units, isolate them, integrate sequentially.
when: Multiple independent fixes, research beside implementation, or a large feature.

steps.title: Define units
steps.body: Each unit needs an outcome, owned files, a verification command and a dependency list.
steps.done: Units do not share writable files or state.

steps.title: Create worktrees
steps.body: One worktree and branch per unit, with an owner. The CLI refuses a dirty tree and enforces the cap.
steps.done: Ownership and scope are recorded.

steps.title: Run and verify
steps.body: Implement in isolation. Each owner runs its unit's checks and records evidence.
steps.done: Each unit has isolated evidence.

steps.title: Integrate sequentially
steps.body: Rebase one unit at a time, resolve conflicts explicitly, and re-run the full gate on the latest target.
steps.done: The integrated revision passes, not just the union of unit tests.

steps.title: Clean up
steps.body: Remove merged worktrees; keep unmerged branches with a reason. Never force-remove dirty work.
steps.done: No orphaned work or shared-state corruption.

title: Prepare a release
summary: Bind a clean revision, passing evidence, version, notes, rollback and artifact digest.
when: A tag, package, binary, container, deployment or store submission.

steps.title: Freeze the candidate
steps.body: Record the exact commit and artifact. Never release from an unverified dirty tree.
steps.done: The candidate digest is recorded.

steps.title: Run the full gate
steps.body: Run the full profile and confirm the evidence record is for this HEAD.
steps.done: The full evidence is pass for the candidate.

steps.title: Check the release contract
steps.body: Check version, changelog, notes, migration and rollback. Verify the artifact hash and any supplied signature/SBOM.
steps.done: The release record is written and reproducible.

steps.title: Get approval and publish
steps.body: Obtain explicit human approval. Publish through the approved channel. Verify the public artifact and smoke-test it.
steps.done: The published digest matches the candidate; rollback is ready.

title: Run many agents in parallel safely
summary: Many agents on many repositories: one task, one worktree, one sandbox, one PR, and a queue instead of collisions.
when: Several agents or sub-agents work at once, share a build machine, or target the same branch.

steps.title: Write the ownership table
steps.body: List each task with its owner, owned paths, verification command and dependencies. No path has two owners; shared files go to one integration owner.
steps.done: A table with no overlapping owned paths is recorded in the work item.

steps.title: Set machine limits
steps.body: Cap concurrent worktrees and build jobs so extra work queues instead of contending. Isolate each task in its own sandbox with scoped, short-lived credentials.
steps.done: The cap, the sandbox definition and the token scopes are written down.

steps.title: Start one worktree per task
steps.body: Each agent gets its own worktree, branch, scope, budget, stop conditions and handoff format.
steps.done: Every running agent maps to exactly one worktree with an owner record.

steps.title: Verify each task on its own
steps.body: Baseline, implement, run the fast gate, then the full gate with the builder and an independent verifier recorded.
steps.done: Each task has full evidence on its own head, verified by a different identity.

steps.title: Land through the queue
steps.body: Merge one change at a time through the merge queue or auto-merge with required checks. Update dependent branches and re-run their gate after each merge.
steps.done: Main stays green; each merged revision has passing gate evidence.

steps.title: Watch by exception
steps.body: Read the digest instead of every run. Clean up finished worktrees.
steps.done: The digest is empty or every item has an owner and a next step.

title: Make a Rust CI fast without lowering the gate
summary: Measure, then cache, link, test and scope smarter — with before/after numbers and the same required checks.
when: Rust builds or CI runs are the bottleneck for agents or reviewers.

steps.title: Baseline
steps.body: Time cold and warm builds and the CI run, per crate and per step, with enough runs to see variance. Record the list of required checks.
steps.done: Before numbers, machine, toolchain and the required-check list are recorded.

steps.title: Add a shared compiler cache
steps.body: Use a compiler cache on S3-compatible storage. Only main-branch CI writes; PR builds and agents read. Separate prefixes per project and toolchain; fixed workdir and path remapping; incremental compilation off in CI.
steps.done: Cache hit rate is recorded in evidence; write credentials exist only in main-branch CI.

steps.title: Faster linker and test runner
steps.body: Try one at a time: a faster linker (mold or lld), then cargo-nextest. Measure each separately. nextest does not run doctests, so keep `cargo test --doc` in the gate.
steps.done: Each change has its own before/after numbers; the test set, doctests included, is unchanged.

steps.title: Scope tests to the change
steps.body: Use the impact list for the fast profile; keep the full suite in the merge gate and heavy suites in nightly.
steps.done: The fast profile states its scope; the full gate still runs everything it ran before.

steps.title: Keep or revert
steps.body: Compare after with before under the same conditions. Keep only changes that are faster with the same checks.
steps.done: Kept changes carry their numbers; anything slower or narrower is reverted.

title: Promote a repository to autopilot
summary: Reduce supervision one tier at a time, one repository at a time, on a week of evidence.
when: Someone proposes letting agents merge or run a repository without per-change review.

steps.title: Check the controls
steps.body: Reproducible environment, passing full profile, tiered CI, merge queue, rollback path, spend cap, alerting, independent verification and a named human. Each needs a link or a command result.
steps.done: A checklist with evidence for every item is in the repository's work item.

steps.title: Rehearse the rollback
steps.body: Revert a harmless change (or redeploy the previous version) and confirm the system returns to the previous state.
steps.done: The rollback was exercised and its evidence is linked.

steps.title: Turn on the digest
steps.body: Deliver `eng digest` daily to the named human and set the budget cap.
steps.done: The human receives the digest and every item has an owner.

steps.title: Promote one tier
steps.body: The owner promotes the repository one tier. Other repositories wait.
commands: gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/rulesets  # confirm required checks and the merge queue
steps.done: The tier decision and date are recorded by the owner.

steps.title: Hold for a week
steps.body: Collect a week of evidence: merges, digest items, reverts and cost. Demote on a failed rollback, an unexplained revert, an overspend or an ignored digest item.
steps.done: A week of evidence shows the tier holds before the next repository is considered.

title: Hardware-in-the-loop (candidate)
summary: Candidate path, not yet exercised: schematics, simulation and a device bench behind the same evidence standard.
when: A project has electronics, firmware or a robot whose behaviour software tests cannot cover.

steps.title: Check the design files
steps.body: Run electrical and design-rule checks and generate fabrication outputs reproducibly from the source files.
steps.done: ERC/DRC results and generated outputs are attached to evidence; nothing is hand-edited.

steps.title: Simulate the circuit
steps.body: Simulate the circuits that matter (power, sensing, drivers) with stated models and limits.
steps.done: Simulation results and the model assumptions are recorded.

steps.title: Emulate the firmware
steps.body: Run firmware tests on an emulator before touching a device.
steps.done: Firmware tests pass in emulation with recorded evidence.

steps.title: Simulate the mechanism
steps.body: For robots, run the controller against a physics simulation with fixed seeds.
steps.done: Simulated runs pass with seeds and tolerances recorded.

steps.title: Run on the bench
steps.body: A self-hosted runner attached to real hardware runs a short, safe test sequence behind a human-approved gate.
steps.done: Bench results are in nightly evidence; a human approved any test that can damage hardware.
